intro: Imagine a theatre so well kept that music still fills it today. You are in Aspendos, an ancient city in Antalya province whose story reaches back to the 5th century BC. Its theatre is the best-preserved of the ancient world, and it still hosts concerts.
history: Aspendos grew rich on the Eurymedon, trading in salt, oil and horses. Its theatre was built by the architect Zeno in the 2nd century. And why does it still stand? Because the Seljuks reused it as a caravanserai, and so the building never fell out of use.
structure-1: You are now in the Roman Theatre, the most completely preserved theatre of antiquity. Notice how the seating bank and the stage building are bonded into a single block. It reached us intact for one simple reason: the Seljuqs kept it in use as a caravanserai.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Aqueducts and the Basilica, then walk on to the Agora and the Stadium.
facts: Did you know? The acoustics are so precise that a whisper on stage reaches the 41st row. This is the best-preserved theatre in the Roman world: the stage building stands to its full height, and concerts are still held here. The architect Zeno is named in an inscription, and a legend tells of a king who promised his daughter to whoever built best, with the theatre winning the prize. The city's aqueduct is one of antiquity's rare pressurised systems, working on the inverted-siphon principle.
outro: This brings our tour of Aspendos to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This theatre has listened for centuries; let it go on listening for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
